title: Oracle Price Change – Reduce Your Oracle Tech Support Bill
description: Oracle recently announced a pricing change that could help you reduce your Oracle costs! You should call up Oracle and get some money back and make sure they don’t charge you on your next renewal.     See our blog post here for more information: https://palisadecompliance.com/reduce-your-oracle-tech-support-bill/

asr.full_text: Hi, this is Craig Rente from Palisade Compliance. And today we want to talk to you about some changes that Oracle has made to their pricing that could help you reduce your tech support costs. Specifically, what Oracle did was they took some formerly extra-cost database options and now they're included for free in the database. The biggest among these are Spatial and Graphical option which used to cost extra, but now it's included. how can this save you money? Well, obviously if you bought it in the past Oracle's not gonna write you a check and give you your money back. However, if you did buy it in the past, you're probably paying for tech support. There's two things we recommend you do. On your next renewal, if you have any of these options licensed, make sure you give Oracle a call and tell them to remove it from your tech support renewal. You shouldn't pay for something that's free. That's number one, and number two, if you already renewed and you have a current support contract with any of those products, then you should also call up Oracle and see if you can get your money back. I mean, after all, Oracle said it's free. So we have a whole blog post on this with details on Oracle's announcements. The challenge here is that Oracle, as far as we can tell, is not proactively reaching out to their clients who have licenses for these products and letting them know that it's now free and letting them know that their support will be reduced. So we estimate that about 7% of Oracle's customers are probably licensed for some of these products. So if you're among that 7%, you should be calling up Oracle right away, get your future support cost down, and maybe even get some money back. If you have problems with Oracle and they're not being responsive or not agreeing to these reductions, please feel free to reach out to us at Palisade compliance, and we'll help you get your money back. Thanks everyone. Have a great day. Happy New Year, and good luck with Oracle.

textual.context: The content presents this as advice about an announced Oracle pricing change. Palisade Compliance also offers assistance if Oracle does not agree to the reductions; whether this is promotional or purely informational is unclear.
textual.potential_relevance: A possible return of money and reduced future costs are linked to the requested action of calling Oracle, with eligibility conditioned on having licensed products or a current support contract and with urgency expressed as calling right away.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish whether Oracle made the stated pricing change, whether any customer qualifies for a refund or reduction, whether Oracle will approve one, or whether the speaker's assistance produces any outcome.

textual_context_notes.observation: The speaker explicitly limits the interpretation of the money-back claim by stating that Oracle would not automatically refund past purchases.

evidence.quote: obviously if you bought it in the past Oracle's not gonna write you a check and give you your money back.

textual_context_notes.observation: The speaker attributes the claimed cost reduction to products that are described as formerly extra-cost options now included in the database.

evidence.quote: they took some formerly extra-cost database options and now they're included for free in the database.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it presents professional guidance about a possible Oracle pricing change and recommends that eligible customers contact Oracle about removing covered items from future support renewals. The invitation to contact Palisade Compliance is framed as assistance with the Oracle dispute, and the discussion explicitly notes that Oracle would not automatically refund past purchases.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The central subject is an ordinary business-service and support-cost matter: customers are advised to contact Oracle about support-renewal pricing and possible refunds, and Palisade Compliance offers assistance with that issue.
